Package fr.sorbonne_u.components.cyphy.interfaces

Interfaces for a cyber-physical component model based on BCM.

See: Description

  • Interface Summary 
    Interface Description
    CyPhyComponentI
    The interface CyPhyComponentI declares the methods that must be implemented by the cyber-physical component.
    CyPhyIntercessionCI
    The class CyPhyIntercessionCI defines the intercession services offered by cyber-physical components in the BCM4Java-CyPhy.
    CyPhyIntrospectionCI
    The interface CyPhyIntrospectionCI extends the standard BCM introspection interface with methods regarding the cyber-physical part of cy-phy components.
    CyPhyReflectionCI
    The interface CyPhyReflectionCI extends the standard BCM feflection interface with methods regarding the cyber-physical part of cy-phy components.
    EmbeddingComponentAccessI
    The interface EmbeddingComponentAccess defines how a simulation model can access its embedding component.
    ModelStateAccessI
    The interface ModelStateAccess defines how a component embedding a simulation model can access a value that resides in the simulation model.
  • Class Summary 
    Class Description
    ModelStateAccessI.VariableValue<T>
    The class VariableValue implements an instantaneous representation of a variable value for NeoSim4Java HIOA models variables; used to exchange values with BCM4Javav-CyPhy cyber-physical components without exposing the actual representation of variable values in NeoSim4Java.

Package fr.sorbonne_u.components.cyphy.interfaces Description

Interfaces for a cyber-physical component model based on BCM.

This software is a computer program whose purpose is to provide an extension of the BCM component model that aims to define a components tailored for cyber-physical control systems (CPCS) for Java.

This package is a part of the BCM4Java-CyPhy framework that integrates DEVS simulation models with the BCM4Java component model. DEVS allows to define modular simulation models that are composed through coupled models by interconnecting them in order to exchange events. They are implemented using the NeoSim4Java framework.

The interfaces defined in this package are Java interfaces either used at the implementation level of BCM to explicit the properties that turn a plain BCM component into a cyber-physical one.

Simulations can be of three main types: model-in-the-loop, software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop. Some interfaces defined in this package helps building software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop by introducing protocols to communicate between components and simulation models.
